## Update your operating system first

At home, update your computer to the latest version of its operating system.

Restart the computer after the update.

::: {.warning}
An outdated system can produce mysterious errors that your classmates do not encounter.
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/01_R_and_RStudio_Installation.Rmd`.
:::

## Install R before installing Positron

1. Go to [cloud.r-project.org](https://cloud.r-project.org/).
2. Choose your operating system.
3. Download and install the current release of R.

If R is already installed, update it before the course begins.

::: {.key-point}
Positron requires R 4.2 or newer.
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Positron installation prerequisites: https://positron.posit.co/install
- The Comprehensive R Archive Network: https://cloud.r-project.org/
:::

## Install Positron

1. Go to [positron.posit.co/install](https://positron.posit.co/install).
2. Choose the installer for your operating system.
3. Accept the licence agreement and follow the standard installation steps.

On macOS, choose the download that matches your computer: **Apple Silicon** or **Intel**.

::: {.key-point}
Install Positron once; it updates itself afterward.
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Install Positron: https://positron.posit.co/install
:::

## Confirm that Positron can run R

Open Positron. In the **Interpreter picker** at the top right, select an R session.

Then run this in the Console:

```{r}
R.version.string
```

You should see an R version of **4.2 or newer** and no error message.

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Managing interpreters in Positron: https://positron.posit.co/managing-interpreters.html
- Discovering R installations: https://positron.posit.co/r-installations.html
:::

## Download and extract the course folder

Download **C407.zip** from **Canvas → Files**.

Extract it to a folder that is easy to find.

::: {.warning}
On Windows, right-click the ZIP file and choose **Extract All…**. Merely opening the ZIP file is not the same as extracting it.
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/01_R_and_RStudio_Installation.Rmd`.
:::

## Check that the data were extracted

In the extracted **C407** folder, open the **Data** folder.

### How many `.rds` files are there?

::: {.answer-grid}
**A.** 1  
**B.** 2  
**C.** 3  
**D.** 4  
**E.** 5
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/01_R_and_RStudio_Installation.Rmd`.
:::

## Open the C407 folder as a workspace

In Positron, choose **File → Open Folder…** and select the extracted **C407** folder.

Opening the folder:

- makes **C407** the workspace;
- shows its files in the Explorer; and
- sets the R working directory to that folder.

::: {.key-point .fragment}
For this course, begin by opening the **C407 folder** in Positron.
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Positron workspaces and R project files: https://positron.posit.co/migrate-rstudio-rproj.html
:::

## Use this start-up routine every class

1. Open **Positron**.
2. Open the **C407 folder** as your workspace.
3. Confirm that an **R interpreter** is active.
4. Open the `.qmd` file used in class.

::: {.key-point}
Keep scripts, data, and outputs together inside the course folder.
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- First data analysis with R in a Quarto document: https://positron.posit.co/tutorial-get-started-quarto.html
- Positron workspaces and R project files: https://positron.posit.co/migrate-rstudio-rproj.html
:::
